record.original_question: For Glauber dynamics at complex fugacity on finite graphs of maximum degree Delta, does there exist a complex domain D_Delta containing [0, 1/(Delta-1)) such that the spectral radius of the transition matrix P (on the quotient space modulo constants) satisfies spr(P)<1 for every such graph whenever w lies in D_Delta?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 There exists a complex domain DDelta containing the interval [0, 1/(Delta - 1) ) such that spr(P) < 1 holds for all graphs G of maximum degree Delta whenever w belongs to DDelta.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Delta \geq 2$ be an integer. For a finite graph $G=(V,E)$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$, consider the hard-core model with complex fugacity $w \in \mathbb{C}$: configurations are independent sets $I \subseteq V$ weighted by $w^{|I|}$. The (single-site) Glauber dynamics is the Markov chain on independent sets of $G$ whose transition matrix $P$ acts as follows: pick a vertex $v \in V$ uniformly at random; if $v$ has no neighbor in the current independent set $I$, set $I' = I \cup \{v\}$ with probability $w/(1+w)$ and $I' = I \setminus \{v\}$ with probability $1/(1+w)$; otherwise set $I' = I \setminus \{v\}$. For complex $w$ the matrix $P$ has complex entries; let $\operatorname{spr}(P)$ denote its spectral radius on the quotient space $\mathbb{C}^{\Omega}/\langle \mathbf{1}\rangle$ (i.e., modulo constants), equivalently the maximum modulus of the non-trivial eigenvalues of $P$.

Question: Does there exist a domain (open connected set) $D_\Delta \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ containing the real interval $[0,\, 1/(\Delta-1))$ such that for every finite graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and every $w \in D_\Delta$, one has
$$\operatorname{spr}(P) < 1\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A direct search did not surface a result that establishes (or refutes) the existence of such a complex contraction domain $D_\Delta$ around the real uniqueness interval $[0, 1/(\Delta-1))$ for Glauber dynamics with complex fugacity. While substantial recent progress on real-fugacity rapid mixing up to the tree-uniqueness threshold has been made (via spectral independence and related techniques), these results concern real $w$ and the spectral gap, not the spectral radius of $P$ on a complex domain. The complex-fugacity contraction conjecture appears to remain unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics via spectral independence for all degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal spectral gap bounds for Glauber dynamics in the tree uniqueness regime (real fugacity).
status_evidence.claim: Recent breakthroughs establish rapid mixing for real fugacity up to uniqueness, but do not address complex-fugacity spectral radius contraction.

status_evidence.title: Rapid Mixing of Glauber Dynamics up to Uniqueness via Contraction
status_evidence.snippet: Proves rapid mixing in the tree uniqueness region for the hardcore model with real fugacity.
status_evidence.claim: Known results concern real fugacity contraction, leaving the complex-domain version unverified in retrieved sources.
